title: If-Then Thinking
summary: If A leads to B, then not B leads to not A, but B does not lead back to A.

steps.title: The puzzle
sentences: If it rains, the match is cancelled.
What can you say about the rain?
points: If it rains, the match is cancelled.

steps.title: How to think about it
sentences: Turn the rule into: rain leads to cancellation.
Then ask what the missing cancellation tells you.
points: Turn the rule into: rain leads to cancellation.

steps.title: The method: The contrapositive
sentences: If rain, then cancelled. The opposite is: if not cancelled, then no rain.
This reversed version is always true when the original is.
points: If rain, then cancelled. The opposite is: if not cancelled, then no rain.

steps.title: The answer
sentences: Since the match was not cancelled, it did not rain.
Be careful: if the match was cancelled, we could not say it rained, because there may be other reasons.
Only the not-cancelled reading is safe.
points: Since the match was not cancelled, it did not rain.

quiz.q: If it is a square, it has four sides. A shape does not have four sides. It is:
quiz.why: No four sides means not a square.
